mechanism_narrative: The steady improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES from t-3w to t-0w signals a gradual return of commuting and daytime population, which lifts weekday retail footfall; therefore RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -38.1 at t-3w to -33.0 at t-0w
fact:WORKPLACES improved from -34.7 at t-3w to -28.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to its last 28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not worsen, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility falls below -10, households are cutting even essential errands, which signals a broad pullback in out-of-home activity that will drag discretionary retail down; RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses below -10.0 but RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks is not lower than its level at the crossing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of positive PARKS mobility and improving TRANSIT indicates that people are both willing to leave home for outdoor leisure and to use public transit; this combined signal should raise retail-and-recreation footfall over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS is positive and TRANSIT improves simultaneously but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a spring transition regime where PARKS mobility turns positive, outdoor foot traffic spills over into nearby retail corridors; RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks as weather improves.
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above 0 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility remaining above +5 indicates continued work-from-home and home-centered routines, which suppresses trips to retail and recreation; RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next week relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 but RETAIL_REC over the next week is not lower than its last four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A policy-driven return-to-office push is visible as a rising WORKPLACES series; when WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week, weekday retail demand increases, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5.0 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -34.7 at t-3w to -28.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises by more than 5.0 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising TRANSIT and falling RESIDENTIAL captures a commuting rebound: as people leave home and use transit, retail corridors regain daytime footfall; RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL falls simultaneously over two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops below -35, it signals renewed travel restrictions or fear-driven avoidance that will reduce discretionary trips; RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next week.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -35.0 but RETAIL_REC over the next week is not lower than its last four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.
